findings.problem: Absence of tanwin is a necessary characteristic of diptotes, not a sufficient diagnostic. The current sentence can force a false diptote tag on a proper name, including the divine name explicitly listed in this same criterion. Its Urdu explanation correctly says many names are diptotes, not all.

counterexamples.metadata: QAC PN, ACC; no tanwin; the divine name is not thereby a diptote.
Prefixed preposition + proper noun in GEN, visible kasra; no tanwin. Lack of tanwin remains insufficient to infer diptote.

findings.currentCriteria: Tag a verb of forms II–X (QAC “(form II)” … “(form X)”) and, when the pattern explains the word’s shape, its participle or verbal noun (مُنذِر، ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ، تَأْوِيل، مُسْتَقِيم). Not for form I verbs, quadriliteral roots, or a shadda that comes from a doubled root (doubled). When the added tāʾ of form V/VI/VIII is changed, merged or dropped, also tag assimilation.

findings.problem: The current shared predicate requires agreement in case and definiteness from a single adjective and from a clause or prepositional-phrase head alike. Agreement of an individual adjective does not transfer to the internally inflected head of a whole attributive clause or phrase. The clause or phrase occupies the syntactic adjectival position as a unit.

counterexamples.metadata: 18:22:2 is explicitly INDEF. 18:22:3 contains a possessive pronoun suffix in genitive idafa and is definite. QAC verse irab explicitly labels the whole رابعهم كلبهم clause a naat of ثلاثة.

findings.currentCriteria: Tag a word, or the head of a clause or prepositional phrase, that the i‘rab calls نعت/صفة of a preceding noun and that agrees with it in case and definiteness. Boundary with haal: an indefinite accusative describing a definite noun is ḥāl; a clause after an indefinite noun is usually ṣifa, after a definite noun usually ḥāl.
findings.exactReplacementCriteria: Tag a word, or the head of a clause or prepositional phrase, that the i‘rab calls نعت/صفة of a preceding noun. For a single-word adjective, apply case and definiteness agreement; for a clause or prepositional phrase, follow the syntactic محل of the modifier as a whole rather than requiring its head word to agree. Boundary with haal: an indefinite accusative describing a definite noun is ḥāl; a clause after an indefinite noun is usually ṣifa, after a definite noun usually ḥāl.
findings.explanationNote: The Urdu card separately introduces a whole clause or prepositional phrase after an indefinite head; the needed definite tagging fix is in the English criterion. Qualifying the opening agreement sentence as single-word would be an optional clarification, not a fourth substantive finding.
